passage: Dilnaz waited until the other children left the counsellor's room. Her voice was small. "Baljeet Ma'am, an older cousin keeps trying to make me sit on his lap and touches me where I don't want. He says it's our secret." She stared at the carpet. "I told my aunt. She said I was imagining it." Baljeet Ma'am put down her pen and moved closer, but not too close. "Thank you for telling me. I believe you. It's not your fault, and it's not a secret you have to keep." She said she would call Dilnaz's mother and the school's safeguarding lead that same day, and she stayed with Dilnaz until they came.

qa.q: What did Dilnaz's aunt say when she first told her?
qa.a: She said Dilnaz was imagining it.

qa.q: Why did Dilnaz stare at the carpet while speaking?
qa.a: She was probably scared and ashamed, and unsure if she would be believed again.

qa.q: What did Baljeet Ma'am do that helped Dilnaz?
qa.a: She said she believed her, that it wasn't her fault and wasn't a secret to keep, then stayed with her and called her mother and the safeguarding lead that same day.

qa.q: What would change if Dilnaz had stopped after her aunt didn't believe her?
qa.a: She might have stayed unsafe and alone, which is why telling again until someone believes you matters. 🤍

grounding: It shows a child reporting unwanted touch and telling again until a trusted adult believes her.

passage:
"Dhruv, can we talk about something important?"
"Is it about homework?"
"No. It's about your body." Sabina sat next to him. "The parts your swimming shorts cover are private. No one should touch them or ask to see them, except a doctor with me there."
"Even family?"
"Even family. And if someone says, 'Keep this secret,' about touching?"
"I tell you."
"Yes. And who else could you tell?"
"Papa. My class teacher."
"And if I don't listen?"
Dhruv thought. "Tell someone else. Keep telling."
"Exactly."

qa.q: What did Sabina say about the parts swimming shorts cover?
qa.a: Sabina said they are private and no one should touch or ask to see them, except a doctor with Sabina there.

qa.q: Why did Dhruv ask "Even family?"
qa.a: He seemed surprised and wanted to check whether the rule applied to people he knows and trusts.

qa.q: What makes Sabina's talk a good way to teach body safety?
qa.a: Sabina uses simple words, lets Dhruv name his own trusted adults and teaches him to keep telling until someone listens.

qa.q: How might Dhruv's class teacher be affected by being on his list?
qa.a: The class teacher becomes one of Dhruv's safe people, so they would need to listen carefully if he ever came to them.

grounding: It shows an adult teaching a child body boundaries, naming trusted adults and telling until believed.

passage: I'm Deepika. Last year, when I was twelve, my friend Tarun stopped wanting to go to his tuition class. He always had an excuse. One evening he told me the tuition teacher had touched him in a way that felt wrong, and said nobody would believe him. My stomach turned over. I remembered what we'd learned in school: private parts are private, and you tell a trusted adult. I said, "I believe you. Let's tell my mother together." We did. My mother listened, then helped his parents go to the school and the police. Tarun doesn't go there anymore. He still says I helped him most by believing him.

qa.q: What did Tarun say the tuition teacher told him?
qa.a: The teacher said nobody would believe him.

qa.q: What does Deepika's stomach turning over show?
qa.a: It shows Deepika was shocked and upset hearing what happened to a friend.

qa.q: What did Deepika do that helped Tarun?
qa.a: Deepika believed Tarun and went with him to tell Deepika's mother, a trusted adult.

qa.q: How might Tarun feel about Deepika now?
qa.a: Tarun feels grateful, saying Deepika helped most by believing him.

grounding: A first-person account of a child believing a friend and helping report abuse to trusted adults.

passage: Counsellor's note, class four, after the body-safety session. At break Ramesh (9) waited until the room emptied. He said an older cousin had been asking him to play a 'secret game' and touched him where his swimsuit covers. Ramesh told him no and went away. He told his mother, but she said, 'Don't make up stories about family.' He said, 'You told us to keep telling until someone believes.' I told him I believed him, that it was not his fault and that he did right to keep telling. I did not ask for details. I informed the principal the same day and followed our school's safeguarding steps, including a call with his father. I will check on Ramesh tomorrow. — Jatin Sir

qa.q: What did Ramesh's mother say when he first told her?
qa.a: She said, 'Don't make up stories about family.'

qa.q: What does Ramesh waiting until the room was empty suggest about how he felt?
qa.a: He was probably scared and embarrassed and needed privacy, but he was determined to be heard.

qa.q: What did Jatin Sir do that was right?
qa.a: He believed Ramesh, told him it wasn't his fault, did not push for details and followed the school's safety steps the same day.

qa.q: How might it feel for Ramesh to hear 'I believe you' after not being believed at home?
qa.a: It would likely bring huge relief and help him trust that telling was worth it. 🤍

grounding: Shows a child who said no to unsafe touch and kept telling trusted adults until he was believed.

passage: Thursday. Today in school we learned the swimsuit rule: nobody can touch the parts a swimsuit covers, and nobody can ask you to keep secrets about touching. Ma'am said good secrets are like surprise parties; bad secrets make your tummy feel wrong. We traced our hands and wrote one trusted adult on each finger. Mine: Mummy, Papa, Baljeet mama, Class Ma'am, and Dadi. Ma'am said if one person doesn't listen, tell the next finger, and the next. I thought about the time Chachi kept squeezing my cheeks and I hated it. Mummy said I'm allowed to say 'no thank you'. I stuck the hand picture on my cupboard. — Lokesh

qa.q: How many trusted adults did Lokesh write on the traced hand?
qa.a: Five: Mummy, Papa, Baljeet mama, Class Ma'am and Dadi.

qa.q: What might Lokesh have been feeling on remembering Chachi squeezing Lokesh's cheeks?
qa.a: Lokesh remembered hating it and was likely relieved to know it is okay to say no to touch that feels unwanted.

qa.q: Why is the 'tell the next finger' idea helpful for children?
qa.a: It shows that if one adult doesn't listen, they should keep telling others until someone helps.

qa.q: How might Lokesh's parents feel seeing the hand picture on the cupboard?
qa.a: They might feel glad Lokesh knows the rules and that they are among the trusted adults on the list.

grounding: A child records learning body-boundary rules and naming trusted adults to tell.
